summary: Rename Django User.note to customer_note in account_user table, preserve GraphQL note field, with zero-downtime concurrent migration: add new column, batched backfill from note to customer_note with convergence guard, deploy new app, retire old app, then drop old column.
write_consistency: During the concurrent window, the old app writes to the note column and the new app writes to customer_note. A batched backfill populates customer_note from note for all existing rows with non-NULL note values before the old app is retired. The note column is retained until after retire_old is deployed, ensuring no existing note values are lost. After retire_old, the note column is safely dropped.
revision_notes: The previous backfill SQL lacked a convergence guard. Added `AND note IS NOT NULL` to the subquery WHERE clause so only rows with actual note values are batched, preventing the infinite re-selection loop caused by updating NULL rows. This allows `repeat_until_zero_rows` to terminate once all non-NULL notes are copied.

stages.description: Add customer_note column to account_user table.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD COLUMN customer_note TEXT NULL;

stages.description: Copy note to customer_note in batches until all rows are updated.
sql: UPDATE account_user SET customer_note = note WHERE ctid IN (SELECT ctid FROM account_user WHERE customer_note IS NULL AND note IS NOT NULL LIMIT 1000);

stages.description: Deploy new app version (new-staged) that uses customer_note column and keeps public GraphQL field note.
Retire old app version that uses note column.
Drop the note column after old app retired.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user DROP COLUMN note;
